newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes rocket south Lebanon for second day.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes rocket south Lebanon for second day.

text.p: Israeli planes raided suspected guerrilla targets in the highlands of south Lebanon for the second successive day on Saturday after guerrillas attacked an Israeli patrol in the region, security sources said.

The planes struck after pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas firing machineguns and anti-tank rockets attacked an Israeli patrol in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
There were no casualties in the guerrilla attack, the sources said.
Israeli gunners responded by pounding suspected guerrilla positions in the Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge with artillery shells.
Two Israeli planes then fired six rockets at the ridge which Hizbollah uses as a base for launching attacks on Israeli troops and their local militia allies in the border occupation zone.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air raid, the second into Lebanon in 1997.

On Friday Israeli warplanes carried out a series of rocket attacks on suspected Hizbollah targets after guerrillas attacked three Israeli outposts in the occupation zone, lightly wounding two soldiers.
